dialogue.speaker: doctor
dialogue.text: When exactly do you normally feel dizzy?

dialogue.speaker: patient
dialogue.text: Mostly when I stand up quickly from a chair or from bed.

dialogue.speaker: parent
dialogue.text: His blood pressure has also been lower than usual when we checked it at home.

dialogue.speaker: doctor
dialogue.text: How long has this been happening?

dialogue.speaker: patient
dialogue.text: About five days. It happened several times yesterday.

dialogue.speaker: doctor
dialogue.text: Have you actually fallen or lost consciousness?

dialogue.speaker: patient
dialogue.text: No. I have not fallen and I have never lost consciousness.

dialogue.speaker: parent
dialogue.text: But yesterday he stood up in the kitchen and nearly lost his balance. I had to hold his arm.

dialogue.speaker: doctor
dialogue.text: Were you having chest pain, palpitations, or shortness of breath at that moment?

dialogue.speaker: patient
dialogue.text: No chest pain and no shortness of breath. I just felt suddenly light-headed.

dialogue.speaker: parent
dialogue.text: He has also been drinking less water recently because he has been very busy at work.

dialogue.speaker: doctor
dialogue.text: Have you started any new medications during the last few weeks?

dialogue.speaker: patient
dialogue.text: No. I have not started any new medication.

dialogue.speaker: doctor
dialogue.text: Okay. I want to check your blood pressure both lying down and standing up, because the timing of the dizziness may be important.
